title: Display & Illumination: WTD MR-16 to std bulb adapter

posts.topic_title: Display & Illumination: WTD MR-16 to std bulb adapter
posts.author: Tony
posts.post_subject: Display & Illumination: WTD MR-16 to std bulb adapter
posts.content_md:
I wonder if anyone knows of an adapter that will screw into a standard light bulb fixture and convert it to an MR-16?

(I know the MR-16 is 12 volt; this thing would have to have a transformer in it like the track lighting kind).

posts.topic_title: Display & Illumination: WTD MR-16 to std bulb adapter
posts.author: BobH
posts.post_subject: Display & Illumination: WTD MR-16 to std bulb adapter
posts.content_md: Have you considered using a PAR-16? It's essentially what you request.

posts.topic_title: Display & Illumination: WTD MR-16 to std bulb adapter
posts.author: Tony
posts.post_subject: Display & Illumination: WTD MR-16 to std bulb adapter
posts.content_md:
The PAR-16 looks bigger, and seems to have a diffuser lens. I like the MR-16 because they're smaller (more like a point source).

I did a Yahoo search on 'MR-16 adapter' and got several hits. Apparently there's a unit that looks like a screw base and has two holes in it to accept the MR-16. I'm going to see if my local electrical supply house has one.

posts.topic_title: Display & Illumination: WTD MR-16 to std bulb adapter
posts.author: Colin Kaminski
posts.post_subject: Display & Illumination: WTD MR-16 to std bulb adapter
posts.content_md: For small holograms I like the MR-12.

posts.topic_title: Display & Illumination: WTD MR-16 to std bulb adapter
posts.author: BobH
posts.post_subject: Display & Illumination: WTD MR-16 to std bulb adapter
posts.content_md: The PAR-16 is the same size as the MR-16 as far as the hologram is concearned. The "16" means both are 16/8ths in diameter. In both cases, the hologram sees a 2" diameter glowing source (regardless of the presence of a diffuser or not), nowhere near a point. The MR-11 is obviously smaller in diameter and is a better choice if used at the same distance.
